# Notes and structure {#notes background-color="#f0674d"}

Where things go, and how the agent keeps track of a project for you.

## Four questions about your project

1. What do you re-explain **every single time**? → the project file.
2. Where does **undone work** live? → a to-do file, not your head or your inbox.
3. Where are you **allowed to be wrong**? → notes, drafts, scratch.
4. What could you **never rebuild**? → raw data, the manuscript. Protect it.

The questions are mine; the answers are yours. Everyone already has a filing
system. It just isn't written down.

## My paper folder

```{=html}
<pre><code>my-paper/
├── AGENTS.md       the rules, for the agent
├── README.md       for people: what this is, how to rerun it
├── STATUS.md       where we are, what's next
├── manuscript/     everything that ends up in the PDF
├── code/           everything that computes
├── results/        the numbers the paper relies on
<b>├── dev/            notes, drafts, talks: in git, not published</b>
<b style="color:#f0674d;">└── local/          downloaded papers, raw runs: not in git</b></code></pre>
```

My four answers: `AGENTS.md`, `STATUS.md`, `dev/`, and `manuscript/` with
`results/`. It's a skill: every new paper starts like this.

## dev/ or local/?

| | In git and on GitHub | Published |
|------------|--------|--------|
| `manuscript/` `code/` `results/` | yes | yes |
| **`dev/`** | yes | no |
| **`local/`{style="color:#f0674d;"}** | [no]{style="color:#f0674d;"} | [no]{style="color:#f0674d;"} |

- **`dev/`** is work in progress: backed up, and your co-authors see it.
- **`local/`{style="color:#f0674d;"}** is listed in `.gitignore`, a text file
  that tells git what to leave alone. PDFs you may not share, big raw files.
- Setting it up: *"Keep local/ out of git."*

## Ask for a structure, not a template

::: {.prompt}
Here is how I work: [your four answers]. Propose a folder structure for this
paper and a project file that says where things go. Show me first; don't move
anything.
:::

Argue with it. Then *"Go ahead"*, and *"Commit"* if you use git.

## Notes the agent keeps for you

::: {.prompt}
At the end of each session, add what we did and what's next to notes/log.md.
:::

::: {.prompt}
Keep literature/notes.md: one paragraph per paper we read, with the pages that matter.
:::

Next time, start with:

::: {.prompt}
Read the project file and the log, then tell me where we left off.
:::

## The project file

`AGENTS.md` in the folder. Both tools read it at every start.

- What the paper is, and where things go.
- The rules, for example:
  - *"Never edit anything in data/raw."*
  - *"Download papers into literature/, or give me the DOI."*
  - *"Only cite references with a verified DOI."*
- Plain text: open it in Notepad and edit it yourself.

More: [the project file](agents.html).

## Skills {#skills}

> Memory is the AI remembering you. A skill is you writing it down.

- A saved workflow with a name and a note on when to use it.
- Worth it for a routine you **repeat**, want done **the same way every time**, or
  want to **hand to a colleague**.
- Make one by asking: *"Turn what we just did into a skill called tidy-paper."*
- You never touch the file format. Most things work fine without skills.
